review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. In the United Republic of Tanzania, UN Women works with the Government of the United Republic of Tanzania, the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar, United Nations agencies, development partners and civil society to advance gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls. In collaboration with the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar and with the support of the Delegation of the European Union, UN Women is implementing the project “Ending Violence against Women and Girls and Advancing Women’s Leadership in Public and Private Sectors in Zanzibar and Mainland”. The project supports the United Republic of Tanzania to deliver on its commitments to gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE), including the roll-out of the National Plan of Action to End Violence against Women and Children (NPA-VAWC 2017–2022 and 2023–2027), the Zanzibar Gender Policy and Generation Equality commitments. Delivery in Zanzibar is carried out jointly with ministries, departments and agencies of the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar, local government authorities and civil society partners across Unguja and Pemba. Reporting to the Program Specialist, Ending Violence against Women and Girls (EVAWG), and working under the functional guidance of the Operations Manager of the Tanzania Country Office, the Program Associate provides operational, administrative and programmatic support to the Zanzibar Office for the development and implementation of effective program, consistent with UN Women rules and regulations. The Program Associate contributes to research, financial management and program implementation, including the processing of program transactions in the corporate ERP system (Quantum), the management of implementing partner agreements, and the coordination of logistics for program activities in Unguja and Pemba. The Program Associate works in close collaboration with the program, operations and project personnel of the Tanzania Country Office, with implementing partners and responsible parties, with counterparts in the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar, and with UN Women Regional Office and Headquarters as required for resolving complex program and finance-related issues and for the exchange of information. Key Functions And Accountabilities Provide administrative and logistical support to the formulation and management of program in EVAWG Programme: Provide administrative support in the preparation of program work plans, budgets, and proposals on program implementation arrangements for the EVAWG portfolio in Zanzibar; Provide administrative and procedural guidance to implementing partners and responsible parties on routine delivery and reporting of program supported activities and finances; Support the preparation, review, amendment and closure of partner agreements, including budget revisions and cost extensions, ensuring completeness and compliance of supporting documentation; Prepare information for the audit of program/projects and support the implementation of audit recommendations; Review and compile program data from program/projects for the Country Office website and for corporate reporting platforms, including the Results Management System (RMS) and UN INFO; Identify sources and gather and compile data and information for the preparation of documents, guidelines, speeches and position papers. Provide administrative support to the financial management of the EVAWG Programme Unit: Create projects in the Quantum system, prepare budget revisions, revise project awards and status, determine unutilized funds, and support the operational and financial closure of projects; Provide administrative support to the monitoring of budget preparation and the finances of program/projects, including the preparation and finalization of Funding Authorization and Certificate of Expenditure (FACE) forms; Review implementing partner financial reports and supporting documentation in line with the Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfers (HACT); follow up on the timely liquidation of advances and support micro-assessments, spot checks and assurance activities; Review financial reports and prepare non-PO vouchers for development projects; Process payments for consultants, service providers, grantees and participants; Maintain the internal expenditure control system and monitor delivery rates against approved annual work plans, alerting the supervisor to over- or under-expenditure; Create requisitions in the Quantum system for development projects and register goods receipts in the Quantum system; Assist in the preparation and follow-up of cost-recovery bills in the Quantum system. Provide administrative support to the EVAWG Programme Unit: Undertake all logistical, administrative and financial arrangements for the organization of meetings, workshops, trainings, community engagements, campaigns, events and missions in Unguja and Pemba; Make travel arrangements for the program team, partners and participants, including travel requisitions, daily subsistence allowance (DSA) processing and travel claims; Prepare public information materials and briefing packets Assemble briefing materials and prepare PowerPoint and other presentations; Participate in joint and technical field monitoring visits; support the documentation of findings and the tracking of follow-up actions and recommendations; Maintain an accurate, complete and secure filing system for program, partner and financial records, and keep partner and stakeholder contact databases up to date; Provide guidance and on-the-job training to Program Assistants, UN Volunteers and interns as needed Provide administrative support to EVAWG Project: Prepare cost-sharing and other agreements; follow up on contributions within the EVAWG resource mobilization efforts; Organize, compile and process information from donors, the EVAWG and the program team, as inputs to various databases and documents; Track donor reporting calendars and support the timely compilation of narrative and financial inputs to donor reports. Facilitate knowledge building and knowledge sharing in EVAWG Programme: Provide administrative support to the synthesis of lessons learned and best practices related to program management and finance; Provide administrative support to the organization of training for office personnel and partners on program and operations related issues; Support the documentation and dissemination of good practices and results from EVAWG interventions in Unguja and Pemba. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Key Performance Indicators: Timely, accurate and compliant processing of program, administrative and financial transactions in Quantum; Full compliance with UN Women rules, regulations, policies and internal controls; audit and spot-check recommendations implemented within agreed timelines; Quality and timeliness of logistical arrangements for meetings, events, trainings and field missions; Accurate and timely entry and maintenance of program and financial data in corporate systems; Quality and timeliness of inputs to donor, corporate and management reports; Positive feedback from the program team, partners and stakeholders on the quality of support and services provided. Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent may provide day-to-day guidance and on-the-job training to Program Assistants and interns and short-term service providers supporting the Zanzibar Office. Competencies : Core Values: Integrity; Professionalism; Respect for Diversity. Core Competencies: Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; Accountability; Creative Problem Solving; Effective Communication; Inclusive Collaboration; Stakeholder Engagement; Leading by Example. Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework: Functional Competencies: Good knowledge of program management and of results-based management principles and tools; Ability to administer and execute administrative and financial processes and transactions; Good knowledge of UN/UN Women financial rules, regulations and implementing partner management procedures, including HACT; Ability to create, edit and present information in clear and presentable formats; Ability to manage data, documents, correspondence and reports, information and workflow; Strong financial and budgeting skills; Strong planning and organizational skills, including event and logistics coordination under tight deadlines; Strong IT skills, including the use of a web-based ERP system and spreadsheet and database packages; Sensitivity to ending violence against women and girls programming, including commitment to confidentiality, survivor-centered approaches and the principle of “do no harm”. review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpa); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The Ebola outbreak in Ituri province (declared mid‑May 2026) is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, with hundreds of suspected cases and dozens of deaths reported across Mongbwalu, Rwampara and Bunia. It began with clusters of unexplained deaths in early May and is spreading in a context of weak health systems, population movement, insecurity, and community mistrust, which together increase the risk of sustained transmission and cross‑border spread to neighbouring countries such as Uganda and South Sudan. The absence of an approved vaccine or specific treatment for this strain makes the outbreak particularly and heightens the urgency of rapid containment. IFRC is scaling up a national society‑led response centered on community engagement, surveillance, and outbreak control, supported by an emergency appeal. Red Cross volunteers are mobilized in affected areas to conduct door‑to‑door awareness, counter misinformation, encourage early care‑seeking, and support safe and dignified burials, key to breaking transmission. At the same time, the IFRC is coordinating closely with governments and partners, strengthening cross-border preparedness, mobilizing resources and surge capacity, and supporting logistics, infection prevention, and community-based surveillance to contain the outbreak and reduce regional spread. The Operations Manager manages the IFRC-coordinated operation. Due to the nature of emergency response operations, this role profile is an outline of the likely responsibilities applicable to the Operations Manager, deployed in a Federation co ordinated operation. The Operations Manager is reporting to the Head of Delegation in Kinshasa and integrates the management team of the delegation. As detailed in IFRC’s Emergency Response Framework (Annex 9 – Detailed Health Co-Leadership Model for Core Functions), the Operations Manager will work closely with the Health Coordinator to ensure co-leadership and direction setting for IFRC’s response to public health emergencies. review_candidates.description: Job Description Summary GE Vernova’s Gas Power business engineers advanced, efficient natural gas-powered technologies and services, along with decarbonization solutions that help enable a lower-carbon future. As a global leader in gas turbines and power plant technologies and services, we are seeking a project Director to lead the execution of Simple and Combined Cycle projects within our Heavy Duty Gas Power business. The Project Director (PD) is responsible for the overall execution of a mega project or multiple projects with a key Customer. Acting as the primary point of contact for the customer, the PD is responsible for the project lifecycle from contract inception through final closure. This role provides the strategic vision required to align complex delivery models with long-term business objectives. By integrating deep operational acumen with a focus on portfolio-level outcomes, the PD influences financial performance, mitigates systemic risks, and serves as a lead mentor, fostering a pipeline of future project leaders and high-performing team members. In addition, in some cases the Project Director serves as a people leader with direct supervisory responsibility for Project Managers, including coaching, performance management, development planning, and team capability building. Job Description Strategic Vision & Portfolio Management Portfolio-Level Outcomes: Manage the interconnected health of multiple projects, ensuring that resources, risks, and performance targets are balanced across the portfolio to drive aggregate business value. Strategic Execution: Define and iterate on long-term project strategies. Shift focus from reactive management to proactive anticipation of market, technical, and customer-driven challenges. Complex Problem-Solving: Serve as the ultimate escalation point for cross-functional bottlenecks. Deploy advanced analytical techniques to resolve high-complexity issues that span engineering, manufacturing, and field execution. Stakeholder Influence: Navigate complex organizational matrices to align diverse internal and external stakeholders toward a unified, long-term vision. Customer Ownership: Develop strong executive relationships to facilitate an open and candid dialogue. Leverage to drive positive outcomes on cross portfolio issue resolution, claims management, and project execution. People Leadership: Directly lead and develop a team of Project Managers. Provide clear priorities, ongoing coaching, performance feedback, development planning, and talent assessment to ensure strong project execution and a robust leadership pipeline. Support employee engagement, accountability, and retention through active people leadership Coaching, Mentorship & Team Development Talent Development: Actively identify and mentor high-potential Project Managers and functional leads. Provide ongoing feedback and career coaching to build a sustainable leadership pipeline. For direct reports, conduct regular performance discussions, assess readiness for expanded scope, and create targeted development actions. Culture of Excellence: Champion a culture of continuous learning and growth. Facilitate knowledge sharing across the project organization to ensure best practices are codified and scaled. Team Empowerment: Coach teams on "influence without authority" and soft-skill development, empowering individuals to take ownership and solve complex problems at their level. Resilience & Well-being: Proactively manage team health by fostering psychological safety and emotional intelligence, ensuring the team remains energized and resilient through high-pressure delivery phases. Financial & Operational Influence Value Stream Optimization: Champion LEAN and Kaizen principles to redesign value streams, eliminating waste and enhancing project efficiency at scale. Financial Stewardship: Proactively influence financial outcomes by optimizing Estimates at Completion (EAC) and Cost-to-Come (CTC) projections. Lead margin maximization efforts through precise control of cash, revenue, and invoicing cycles. Contractual & Claims Strategy: Lead negotiations on complex change orders and vendor claims, utilizing a strategic approach to protect project interests while maintaining robust customer relationships. Risk, EHS & Integration Risk & Opportunity Architecture: Own the portfolio Risk & Opportunity register. Quantify risks not just for individual tasks, but for the overall project outcome. EHS & Quality Leadership: Enforce a "zero-compromise" culture regarding EHS and quality standards, regardless of pressure to accelerate schedules. Qualifications & Competencies Education: Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university. Experience: 10+ years of experience leading mega-projects or complex portfolios within the Energy or large-scale infrastructure sectors. Strategic Acumen: Demonstrated ability to translate complex business challenges into clear, actionable, and sustainable project strategies. People Leadership / Mentorship Record: Proven experience in developing talent, coaching project teams, and building a high-performance culture within a matrixed organization. Experience with performance management, employee development, and leading Project Managers or comparable professional roles is preferred. Problem-Solving Mastery: Proven record of identifying systemic issues and implementing solutions across interdependent workstreams. Executive Presence: Advanced ability to represent the organization at the C-Suite level, facilitating high-stakes negotiations and managing sensitive customer communications.
